newsitem.title: USA: Former financial advisor charged in fraud.
newsitem.headline: Former financial advisor charged in fraud.

text.p: A former financial advisor and principal owner of Mutual Financial Services has been arrested on charges relating to an alleged scheme to defraud school teachers of more than $500,000 in retirement savings, federal prosecutors said Monday.

Wayne Drinkwine, 44, of Riverhead, N.Y., was arrested Friday on a 22-count indictment that charges him with mail fraud and perjury in testimony before the Securities and Exchange Commission in connection with an SEC civil suit against him.
If convicted, he faces a possible maximum prison term of five years on each of the counts and fines of up to $250,000 on each charge.

According to the indictment, Drinkwine met with teachers from New York's Westchester County and Long Island and Connecticut school districts to provide individual retirement planning and investment advice.
Drinkwine opened brokerage accounts for the teachers and earned commissions from securities transactions in those accounts, the indictment charged.

Beginning in 1990, he allegedly encouraged certain teachers to invest in "unit trust" real estate investments through his company, located in Ronkonkoma, N.Y. He allegedly guaranteed that these investments would generate a 10 percent return without risk to the principal.
The indictment alleged that five teachers entrusted more than $500,000 to Drinkwine to invest in unit trusts, which represented the majority of their retirement savings.
He allegedly diverted the funds to his own use.
It was further charged that in 1992 and 1994, Drinkwine received more than $30,000 from three teachers to invest in certain stocks and annuities he recommended.
The indictment alleged that Drinkwine also diverted the funds to his own use.
He is also charged with lying to the SEC in June while he was questioned as part of its civil suit against him.
